subject: Re: Clarifying discounts — AWS Marketplace vs direct billing for Hosted API commits
messages:
From: Claire Nolan <claire.n@acme-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <aws-portal@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Pricing ask — commit tiers and Marketplace billing implications

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising. Our procurement team is asking for a clear comparison: if we do a usage-based commit with Redwood Hosted API, how do discounts change if we purchase via AWS Marketplace versus direct invoicing?

Specifically:
- For a $50k/month committed spend, what discount would apply per-token under direct billing vs marketplace?
- Are there profile differences (tier definitions, overage handling) we should know about?
- How will monthly invoicing and reconciliation differ (we need month-end invoices tied to AWS Marketplace billing line items)?

Procurement asked to loop in docs and any sample SOW / T&Cs for Marketplace purchases. Can you send a short overview we can pass to ops?

Appreciate it — Claire

Attachment: none in this message
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nolan <claire.n@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pricing ask — commit tiers and Marketplace billing implications

Claire — thanks, great questions. Short version up front: you can get equivalent list discounts on committed Hosted API spend, but Marketplace purchases typically reduce the effective discount off list because the cloud marketplace takes a portion of gross revenue and billing flows through their metering; the pass-through is imperfect. Details below.

High-level differences:
- Direct billing (invoiced by Redwood):
  - We can offer a straightforward volume-discount schedule tied to per-token usage and explicit commit tiers.
  - Discounts apply directly to list per-token rates; overages billed at agreed overage rate.
  - Invoicing ties to Redwood account; simpler reconciliation for credits/adjustments.
- AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace:
  - Marketplace listing has price we set, but marketplace fees (~5–15% depending on program/region) mean Redwood often offers a slightly different net margin to keep the marketplace listing competitive. 
  - Discounting often gets handled as a commitment rebate or via price tiers inside the marketplace listing — this can limit how we structure complex volume tiers or retroactive true-ups.
  - Invoicing is through the marketplace (customer sees AWS invoice), which helps procurement but complicates immediate vendor-side credits.

Numbers (examples for $50k/month commit, Hosted API per-token model):
- Direct invoiced commit: 20% off list per-token for $50k/month committed spend, with standard overage at 80% of list.
- AWS Marketplace purchase: equivalent gross discount to customer ends up around 12–15% in many deals after marketplace fees and listing constraints — we can negotiate higher by structuring a Marketplace Private Offer, but that requires AWS procurement flow and longer lead time.

We can support these options:
1) Direct invoice: fastest, most flexible for complex rollouts, supports retroactive true-ups and clean overage handling.
2) Marketplace Private Offer: we can craft a private listing with a negotiated price/discount; typically takes 1–2 weeks to set up and procurement routes through AWS console.

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with modeled examples across commit sizes and both purchase routes. Also attaching the current terms (redwood_terms_v3.pdf) — note legal differences for Marketplace purchases are minor but procurement will see the vendor/invoice as AWS.

Next steps: tell me whether Procurement prefers Marketplace line-item billing (they mentioned month-end reconciliation) or if they prefer direct invoice with Redwood PO processing. Happy to set up a short sync with your procurement lead + our sales ops.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx (spreadsheet); redwood_terms_v3.pdf (pdf)

Sean/Claire,

We generally prefer AWS Marketplace billing to keep all software spend on our consolidated invoice, but we're open to a direct vendor relationship if the economics are materially better. A few procurement notes:
- Can you provide a Marketplace Private Offer? If so, can the price be locked for 12 months?
- Need a sample monthly invoice line example (how the usage shows up in the AWS bill).
- Any SSO/tenant mapping requirements for metering (we need the mapping documented for our finance team).

If you can share the above and the sample private offer ID, we can route for approvals next week.

Procurement Team
Acme Analytics
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:40:00 -0500
Subject: Internal: Recommended offer structure for Acme — marketplace vs direct

Sean — quick internal note so you're aligned for the procurement call:

Recommendations:
- Offer a 22% direct-invoice discount at $50k/mo commit (we can absorb in ARR economics), with a 1% monthly true-up credit if usage exceeds the commit by >10% for the quarter.
- For Marketplace: propose a Private Offer at a 16% list discount equivalent (net to customer ~14% after AWS fees) and include a 12-month price lock; require procurement to accept Private Offer terms to enable the pricing.
- Include a clause for a migration path: 30-day notice to move from Marketplace to direct billing once procurement has setup vendor PO if they want refunds/true-ups applied more cleanly.

Rationale: direct gives better flexibility for overage true-ups and credits; Marketplace is easier for procurement but reduces our margin — the Private Offer bridges both options.

Flag for legal: need to confirm marketplace price-lock language and whether we can add the migration clause. Markus, can you check w/ legal and confirm if adding a migration path is acceptable?

Thanks — Ava
Product GTM, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nolan <claire.n@acme-analytics.com>, Procurement <aws-portal@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing ask — commit tiers and Marketplace billing implications

Claire/Team — following up after internal alignment. Two concrete paths:

1) Direct Redwood invoice (recommended if you need flexible true-ups):
   - $50k/mo commit => 22% off list per-token rates
   - Overage rate = 85% of list per-token
   - Quarterly true-up credit process included in SOW
   - We issue monthly invoice; finance can pay via Redwood PO.

2) AWS Marketplace Private Offer (recommended if you must have AWS consolidated billing):
   - Private Offer: 16% off list in the listing (net to you ~14% after marketplace fees)
   - 12-month price lock available on Private Offer
   - Metering lines show usage per product id in AWS bill; we will provide mapping doc and sample invoice line.

Attachments: updated pricing workbook and our terms (same attachments as earlier).

If Procurement is comfortable with a Private Offer, I'll kickoff the AWS Private Offer process and loop in Sales Ops — we typically need PO info and a signed acceptance in the AWS console. If they prefer direct, I can send a PO + SOW template for signature and route to RevOps.

Would you like a 30-minute call Monday to finalize?

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
